To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

kurtosis is a vague concept that can be formalized by partial orderings on probability distributions, the measures that preserve these orderings and the scale matching techniques used to place shoulders in the distributions.

kurtosis is best defined in terms of location- and scale-free partial orderings, that it is best expressed in terms such as “a distribution is less peaked than another,” and that it is best understood by recognizing that the formalizations of kurtosis that have appeared in literature are all special cases of a general definition that is based on the location- and scale- free partial ordering of distributions and the measures of kurtosis are all special cases that preserve this ordering.

(i) kurtosis is the location and scale-free movement of probability mass away from the shoulders of the distribution into its center or tails and (ii) kurtosis can be formalized by partial orderings on probability distributions and measures that preserve them

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
kurtosis is a measure of the extent to which the tails of a distribution are fatter or thinner than those of a reference distribution.
kurtosis is a vague concept that can be formalized and that it is a measure of the location and scale freedom of the movement of probability mass into a distribution's center and tails.

The main takeaway from our work is that
there is no single definition of kurtosis that is best.
there is no unique formalization of the concept and that the choice of formalization is dictated by the context in which it will be used.
kurtosis is best understood as the location and shape free movement of probability from the shoulders of distributions into their center and tails.
